title: An element good with respect to a maximal regular sequence of a Cohen–Macaulay module is a nonzerodivisor
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$). For a finite $R$-module $N$ let $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, $N_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\dots\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ ($-\infty$ when $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\emptyset$, i.e. $N=0$; the same definition for any subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in place of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$). For elements $a_1,\dots,a_k\in R$ let $V(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ be the set of prime ideals of $R$ containing all $a_j$. Let $M\neq0$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth]; let $d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, an integer $\ge0$, and let $f_1,\dots,f_d\in\mathfrak m$ be an $M$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $d$. Let $g\in\mathfrak m$ be *good* with respect to $(M,f_1,\dots,f_d)$, that is, $\dim\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g,f_1,\dots,f_i)\bigr)=d-i-1$ for every $i=0,1,\dots,d-1$. Then (a) $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $g$ on $M$ is injective), and (b) $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay, $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=d-1$, and $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}$ is an $M/gM$-regular sequence (a maximal one, its length being $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)$).
